hook: One night of poor sleep reduces activity in the prefrontal cortex by up to 30%. That is the part of your brain responsible for every decision you make tomorrow.
topic: Sleep deprivation and prefrontal cortex function — cognitive cost made concrete
body:
**The prefrontal cortex is responsible for planning, decision-making, impulse control, and working memory. It is the part of the brain that makes you effective, rational, and regulated. It is also the part of the brain most sensitive to sleep deprivation.**

After a single night of disrupted sleep, prefrontal activity decreases significantly. The amygdala — which handles threat detection and emotional reaction — shows the opposite pattern. It becomes hyperreactive, and the inhibitory connection between it and the prefrontal cortex weakens.

The practical result: you are less able to think clearly, more reactive to minor stressors, more impulsive, and less able to catch yourself before a bad decision. And critically — the research consistently shows that sleep-deprived individuals rate their own performance as roughly normal. The impairment degrades your ability to perceive the impairment.

This is why "I function fine on six hours" is almost always inaccurate. Not as an opinion — as a measurable neurological fact.

You don't feel as impaired as you are. That is the mechanism. And it matters.

Full breakdown is linked in my bio.
